clips.title: Terraform Basics: Modules
clips.why: Ned explains what a module is and why you write one: the same group of resources, reused with different inputs.
look: A module is a folder of .tf files; the folder you run is the root module.
Child modules are called with a module block and a source.
Why reuse matters: the same shape in more than one place.
clips.after: Our three sandbox modules (the private VPC, the pool and the proxy) are called by Terragrunt units in exactly this way.

clips.title: Terraform Basics: Modules
clips.why: The other edge of the contract: what a module gives back with outputs, and how the caller reads them.
look: An output has a name and a value.
The caller reads it as module.<name>.<output>.
clips.after: Other units read our pool module's outputs, such as the group names, through a Terragrunt dependency.

clips.title: Simplify your Terraform code w/ "for_each"
clips.why: for_each over a map variable, step by step: one resource per key, configured from the value.
look: The map variable that holds the different settings.
each.key and each.value inside the resource.
How the plan names each resource by its key.
clips.after: Our launch templates and groups use for_each over the sizes map, so each key, lite, full or wide, is an identity.

clips.title: Validate your code with the Terraform test framework
clips.why: HashiCorp's short introduction to the test framework you use in the lab: test files, run blocks, assertions and running the tests.
look: The test file and its run blocks.
A unit test with command = plan, so nothing is created.
The output of running the tests.
clips.after: OpenTofu has the same framework, so tofu test proves a pool module change before any plan reaches a reviewer.

practice.q: In the group block, pick the template of the same size.
practice.hint: Inside a for_each block, which value names the current entry of the map?
practice.why: each.key is lite, full or wide. Both blocks use the same keys, so this finds the template of the group's own size.

practice.q: Which expression gives { full = "m8i.2xlarge", lite = "m8i.xlarge" } from var.sizes with three sizes?

options.text: [for k, v in var.sizes : v if k != "wide"]
options.why: Square brackets make a list of values, so you lose the keys that for_each needs.

options.text: { for k, v in var.sizes : k => v if k != "wide" }
options.why: Braces build a map, k => v keeps each entry, and the if drops wide.
merge keeps the key wide, with a null value. for_each would still see three keys, or fail on the null.

practice.q: Add the account tags first and the sweeper's tag on top, so the sweeper always finds the VM.
practice.hint: The function that combines maps; the later map wins.
practice.why: merge() combines maps, and for the same key the later map wins, so the module's own tag can never be lost or overwritten by the account's tags.

practice.q: Put a safe module change in order.
items: Read variables.tf and outputs.tf to learn the contract
Try new expressions in tofu console
Make the change, keeping existing keys and variable names
Run tofu test in the module folder
Plan a unit that uses the module and read every replace and destroy
practice.why: The contract tells you what you must not break, the console and the tests catch logic mistakes early, and the plan of a real caller shows what would happen to things that already exist.

practice.q: You must add a new input to a module that ten units already use. Which change will not break any of them?

options.why: No default means every existing caller must now set it, so each of their plans fails until they do.

options.text: Rename warm_pool_size to warm_pools and add the new input
options.why: The rename alone breaks every unit that sets warm_pool_size.
An optional variable with a default keeps the contract: old callers keep working, new callers can opt in.
